standard_prerequisites: Cohomology of Spaces, proper pushforward of a coherent module is coherent, and every coherent sheaf on a good algebraic space is the pushforward of a coherent module on a closed subspace that is its support

The closed immersion case of the cycle class computation for a pushforward, and the identification of the k-dimensional part of a cycle class with a sum over the irreducible components of delta-dimension k
Spaces over Fields, finiteness in codimension 1 near a generic point of a component, and Chow Homology's cycle pushforward lemma for schemes, used as the final reduction step
core_obligations: Part (1) is reduced to part (2) by applying the closed subspace case to the closed subspace with the same delta-dimension bound

For part (2) replace the coherent sheaf by a coherent module on its support Z, form the scheme theoretic image Z' of the restriction of f to Z, and use the resulting commutative square together with the two pushforward computations to reduce the equality to the cases of a closed immersion and of the restricted morphism
Settle the closed immersion case from the length statement and the definitions, and thereby reduce to the situation where the delta-dimension of X is at most k and f is proper and surjective

In that situation show that every component occurring in either cycle class is an irreducible component of Y of delta-dimension k, and that its generic point lifts to a generic point of a component of X of the same delta-dimension
Use finiteness in codimension 1 to pass to an open subspace over which the morphism is finite, shrink to an affine base, and invoke the scheme case of the cycle pushforward lemma
proof_roadmap: Reduce part (1) to part (2) using the closed subspace case
Apply the support decomposition and the scheme theoretic image diagram to reduce to a closed immersion and to the restriction of f to the support
From the closed immersion case reduce to f proper and surjective with the delta-dimension of X at most k
Compare the components appearing in both cycle classes, then shrink to a finite morphism over an affine open and quote the scheme case
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the two-part lemma at source lines 1020-1040, label lemma-cycle-push-sheaf, whose proof (source lines 1042-1119) is a two-stage reduction: the second part is first reduced to a closed immersion through the support decomposition of a coherent sheaf and the scheme theoretic image square of the restriction of f to the support, with the equalities pushed through the diagram f_* i_* = i'_* (f|_Z)_*, and then, after the closed immersion case, to the situation where the delta-dimension of X is at most k and f is proper and surjective, where the solver must show that the components occurring in either cycle class are exactly the components of Y of delta-dimension k and that their generic points lift, before shrinking to a finite morphism over an affine open and quoting the scheme case. The counted statement records neither the diagram nor the component comparison, and several steps are controlled by prerequisites that are delivered as navigation pointers.
